item.A:
No. `let b = a;` moves the `String` into `b`, so `a` can't be used afterwards (error E0382, *borrow of moved value*).
With `let b = a.clone();` it compiles.

item.Q: At any one time, a value may have either {{c1::any number of shared references}} or {{c2::exactly one mutable reference}}.
Why does `let y = x;` leave `x` usable when `x` is an `i32`?
item.A: `i32` is `Copy`, so the value is copied instead of moved.
